items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: Victor Rendon is a percussionist who I believe lives in Brooklyn

ctx.x: I guess the biggest thing would be putting myself in the zone of what they were doing, adapting, listening, of course listening is a huge part of any musical study. Spending — a big thing for me has always been spending time with the people as people and not just running in, absorbing the music and taking off you know. It’s been a bit of a 24/7. You go over there you’re drinking some rum with them and then the music activity happens and then you’re spending more time with them afterwards and say, “Ah — I’ll see…

I’d like to read something here. Victor Rendon is a percussionist who I believe lives in Brooklyn and he’s the leader of the Bronx Conexion Latin-Jazz Big Band. And I asked him a similar question about learning it and he said, and I’ll paraphrase here, in Cuba it’s by rote. It’s an oral tradition what they do, the novice would basically sit there or maybe stand against the wall and listen, pick it up by ear. If they were not an annoyance they would let you stay there and then maybe you would get to play.

Yeah. That’s right on. I totally hear him, yeah that’s exactly what it is like. Yeah. I mean and that’s not, you know, that’s not far off from the early jazz traditions too right? You know getting up on the bandstand and if you suck you’re off. If you even get that opportunity.
